subject.title: SecretRef credentials travel as plaintext through the model-call chain after resolution

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the linked process-local sentinel and egress-injection design for SecretRef-managed model credentials, or require a narrower staged hardening plan first?
rationale: The plaintext propagation is source-supported, but the proposed remedy changes cross-cutting credential handling and provider adapter behavior under a security-sensitive boundary.

options.title: Review the linked sentinel PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102009 as the canonical fix candidate and require security, compatibility, adapter-boundary, and live leak-sweep proof before merge.

options.title: Stage a narrower first fix
options.body: Ask for a smaller initial hardening step such as exact-value redaction plus guarded-fetch convergence, with full sentinels left for a follow-up.

options.title: Keep the documented process boundary
options.body: Accept current same-process plaintext exposure for now and defer stronger isolation to an external credential proxy or later plugin/API design.

recommendation.title: Review the linked sentinel PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102009 as the canonical fix candidate and require security, compatibility, adapter-boundary, and live leak-sweep proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history for SecretRef and auth-profile resolution, which is the first boundary touched by this decision.
